subproblem.title: C^1 approximation of Lipschitz functions (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5)
subproblem.statement: Let n be a natural number, f : R^n -> R Lipschitz (with constant K >= 0) and eps > 0. Then there is a C^1 function g : R^n -> R such that L^n({x : f(x) != g(x)} union {x : Df(x) != Dg(x)}) < eps, where L^n is Lebesgue measure (volume) on R^n = EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) and Df(x) = fderiv R f x (the zero map at points where f is not differentiable).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (f : Rn n → ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0), LipschitzWith K f → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ g : Rn n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ volume ({x | f x ≠ g x} ∪ {x | fderiv ℝ f x ≠ fderiv ℝ g x}) < ENNReal.ofReal ε
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the printed proof of Simon, Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5 (pp. 42-44), with the measure-theoretic details filled in. The parent proof (step 1) cites this theorem; it is proved here once.
Notation: L^n = volume on R^n; |.| Euclidean norm; for k >= 1 write S_k := {x : k - 1 <= |x| < k} (Borel, bounded, pairwise disjoint, union R^n). For x where f is differentiable write Df(x) for its derivative (a linear map R^n -> R).
1. (Rademacher.) The set B := {x : f is differentiable at x} is Borel (Mathlib measurableSet_of_differentiableAt) and L^n(R^n \ B) = 0 by Rademacher's theorem (Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt; SimonGMT Chapter02.rademacher_ae_differentiableAt). The map x -> Df(x) = fderiv R f x is Borel measurable (Mathlib measurable_fderiv).
2. (Lusin on bounded pieces.) Fix k >= 1. A_k := B cap S_k is Borel with L^n(A_k) < infinity. L^n restricted to a bounded set is a finite Borel measure on a metric space, hence weakly regular (Mathlib Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure). By weak regularity choose a closed set C_k^0 contained in A_k with L^n(A_k \ C_k^0) < eps 2^{-k-2}/(n+1) (Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt). For q = 1..n apply Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable) to the Borel real function x -> Df(x)(e_q) on A_k with tolerance eps 2^{-k-2}/(n+1): this gives a closed set C_k^q contained in A_k with L^n(A_k \ C_k^q) < eps 2^{-k-2}/(n+1) and x -> Df(x)(e_q) continuous on C_k^q. Put C_k := C_k^0 cap C_k^1 cap ... cap C_k^n (for n = 0 this is just C_k^0). Then C_k is closed, contained in A_k, L^n(A_k \ C_k) < eps 2^{-k-2}, and Df restricted to C_k is continuous (a map into the finite-dimensional space of linear maps R^n -> R is continuous iff its coordinates Df(.)(e_q) are; for n = 0 that space is a single point). Put C := union_k C_k. Since C_k is contained in the bounded set S_k, every bounded set meets only finitely many C_k; hence C is closed (locally finite union of closed sets) and Df restricted to C is continuous (each point has a neighbourhood meeting only finitely many of the closed sets C_k, and Df is continuous on each of them, so the pasting lemma applies). Moreover C is contained in B and L^n(R^n \ C) <= L^n(R^n \ B) + sum_k L^n(A_k \ C_k) <= sum_{k>=1} eps 2^{-k-2} = eps/4.
3. (The remainder functions.) For x != y in C put R(x, y) := (f(y) - f(x) - Df(x)(y - x))/|y - x|. For k >= 1 and x in C let phi_k(x) := sup({0} union {|R(x, y)| : y in C, 0 < |y - x| < 1/k}); put phi_k := 0 off C. Since f is K-Lipschitz, |R(x, y)| <= K + ||Df(x)||, so 0 <= phi_k(x) < infinity; phi_{k+1} <= phi_k; and phi_k(x) -> 0 as k -> infinity for every x in C, because f is differentiable at x (C is contained in B). Measurability: let D be a countable dense subset of C. For fixed x in C the set {y in C : 0 < |y - x| < 1/k} is relatively open in C, hence D is dense in it, and y -> |R(x, y)| is continuous on it (f continuous, denominator nonzero); therefore phi_k(x) = sup({0} union {|R(x, y)| : y in D, 0 < |y - x| < 1/k}). For each fixed y in D, x -> |R(x, y)| times the indicator of {x in C : 0 < |y - x| < 1/k} is Borel (Df Borel, f continuous, C closed). So phi_k is a countable supremum of Borel functions, hence Borel.
4. (Egorov on bounded pieces.) Fix k >= 1. C cap S_k has finite measure, phi_j are Borel and phi_j -> 0 pointwise on C cap S_k. By Egorov's theorem (Mathlib tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto' applied to L^n restricted to C cap S_k) there is a Borel set E_k contained in C cap S_k with L^n((C cap S_k) \ E_k) < eps 2^{-k-2} and phi_j -> 0 uniformly on E_k as j -> infinity. Put A_0 := union_k E_k. Then L^n(C \ A_0) <= sum_k eps 2^{-k-2} = eps/4, and since a bounded set meets only finitely many S_k, phi_j -> 0 uniformly on every bounded subset of A_0 (a finite union of sets of uniform convergence).
5. (A closed set.) For each k choose, by weak regularity of L^n restricted to the bounded set E_k (Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt), a closed set F_k contained in E_k with L^n(E_k \ F_k) < eps 2^{-k-2}. Put A := union_k F_k; A is closed (F_k is contained in S_k, so the union is locally finite), A is contained in A_0, contained in C, contained in B, and L^n(A_0 \ A) <= eps/4. Hence L^n(R^n \ A) <= L^n(R^n \ C) + L^n(C \ A_0) + L^n(A_0 \ A) <= 3 eps/4 < eps.
6. (Whitney's hypothesis.) Let h := f and xi := Df on A. h is continuous on A (f Lipschitz) and xi is continuous on A (A contained in C, step 2). Let K' be a compact subset of A and eta > 0. K' is bounded, so by step 4 there is j with phi_j < eta on K'. Then for x in K' and y in A with |y - x| < 1/j: if y != x, |f(y) - f(x) - Df(x)(y - x)| = |R(x, y)| |y - x| <= phi_j(x)|y - x| <= eta|y - x| (y is in A, contained in C); if y = x the inequality is trivial. This is exactly the hypothesis (*) of Whitney's extension theorem (Simon Ch. 2, 1.6), i.e. HasWhitneyC1Compatibility A h xi in SimonGMT (continuous value, continuous derivative, remainder with delta = 1/j).
7. (Whitney extension and conclusion.) By Whitney's extension theorem (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.6; SimonGMT Chapter02.exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney) there is g in C^1(R^n) (ContDiff R 1 g) with g = f on A and HasFDerivAt g (Df(a)) a for every a in A; hence Dg(a) = Df(a) for a in A. Therefore {f != g} union {Df != Dg} is contained in R^n \ A, whose measure is < eps by step 5. (If A is empty the extension is any C^1 function, e.g. 0, and the same inclusion holds.) This proves the claim.
proof_key_steps: Rademacher: f is differentiable off an L^n-null Borel set B^c, and Df is Borel
Lusin on the bounded shells: a closed C contained in B with Df continuous on C and L^n(R^n \ C) <= eps/4
The difference quotients phi_k (countable sup over a dense subset, hence Borel) decrease to 0 on C
Egorov on the shells: phi_k -> 0 uniformly on bounded subsets of A_0, L^n(C \ A_0) <= eps/4
Inner regularity: a closed A contained in A_0 with L^n(R^n \ A) < eps
Whitney's C^1 compatibility holds on A; Whitney extension gives g in C^1 with g = f and Dg = Df on A

audit.reason: The prose and standalone Lean proposition agree, including derivative agreement and n = 0. Locally finite shell constructions produce closed sets with the stated loss bounds. The countable-supremum argument establishes measurability, and Egorov supplies compact-uniform Whitney compatibility. Whitney extension then proves both required agreements. This is a complete, non-circular proof.

subproblem.title: Approximate tangent spaces of a bi-Lipschitz C^1 chart image, with continuous projection field (parent step 2)
subproblem.statement: Let n >= 1, l >= 0, G : R^n -> R^(n+l) a C^1 map, c in R^n, rho in R and kappa > 0, and let B' := B'_rho(c) be the open ball. Assume DG(v) is injective for every v in B' and kappa|v - w| <= |G(v) - G(w)| for all v, w in B'. Let N := G(B'). Then N is Borel, H^n(N) < infinity, and there is a map T from R^(n+l) to the linear subspaces of R^(n+l) such that x -> p_{T(x)} (orthogonal projection onto T(x), a continuous linear map) is continuous on N, and for every x in N, T(x) is the approximate tangent space of N at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4 (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x (T x): dim T(x) = n and lim_{r -> 0+} int_{eta_{x,r}(N)} f dH^n = int_{T(x)} f dH^n for every f in C_c(R^(n+l))).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} (G : Rn n → Amb n ℓ) (c : Rn n) (ρ κ : ℝ), 1 ≤ n → ContDiff ℝ 1 G → 0 < κ → (∀ v ∈ ball c ρ, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ G v)) → (∀ v ∈ ball c ρ, ∀ w ∈ ball c ρ, κ * ‖v - w‖ ≤ ‖G v - G w‖) → MeasurableSet (G '' ball c ρ) ∧ (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (G '' ball c ρ) < ⊤ ∧ ∃ T : Amb n ℓ → Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), ContinuousOn (fun x => (T x).starProjection) (G '' ball c ρ) ∧ ∀ x ∈ G '' ball c ρ, Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (G '' ball c ρ) x (T x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 2 ('Blow-ups of N_k') together with the measurability/finiteness facts of step 1, for a single chart. Notation and conventions (shared): H^n = muHE[n] (Mathlib's normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure; on R^n it equals Lebesgue measure L^n = volume, Mathlib InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, and on an n-dimensional subspace P it is n-dimensional Lebesgue measure on P, so H^n(P cap B_s(0)) = omega_n s^n). Balls B_s(y) are closed, B'_s(y) open. eta_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y - x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). For r > 0, eta_{x,r} is a homeomorphism (a similarity with ratio 1/r), H^n(eta_{x,r}(S)) = r^{-n} H^n(S) for every set S, and the pushforward of H^n restricted to eta_{x,r}(S) under eta_{x,r}^{-1}(y) = x + r y is r^{-n} H^n restricted to S (SimonGMT Chapter04 hausdorff_blowUp_image, map_inverse_blowUp_carrier). Consequently, for every set S and every function h (Bochner integrals, the identity holding exactly, including the value 0 for non-integrable integrands, because it comes from a measurable embedding and a scalar multiple of a measure):
(CV) int_{eta_{x,r}(S)} h(y) dH^n(y) = r^{-n} int_S h(eta_{x,r}(z)) dH^n(z), and H^n(eta_{x,r}(S) cap B_R(0)) = r^{-n} H^n(S cap B_{rR}(x)).
JG(v) := normDet(DG(v)) = (det(DG(v)^* DG(v)))^{1/2} (SimonGMT areaJacobianAt G v).
0. (Trivial case.) If rho <= 0 then B' and N are empty: N is Borel with H^n(N) = 0, and any T works (continuity on the empty set and the tangent condition are vacuous). Assume rho > 0 from now on.
1. (Bounds.) The closed ball B := B_rho(c) is compact and v -> DG(v) is continuous (G is C^1), so Lambda := sup_B ||DG|| < infinity and J* := sup_B JG < infinity (JG is continuous because normDet is continuous, SimonGMT Chapter02.continuous_normDet). By the mean value inequality on the convex set B', G is Lambda-Lipschitz on B'.
2. (Inverse chart.) Because kappa > 0, the lower bound shows G is injective on B'. Let psi : N -> B' be the inverse of G restricted to B'. For x = G(v), x' = G(v') in N: |psi(x) - psi(x')| = |v - v'| <= kappa^{-1}|x - x'|; so psi is Lipschitz, in particular continuous on N.
3. (N Borel, finite measure.) B' is open in R^n, hence sigma-compact (B' = U_m B_{rho - 1/m}(c)); G is continuous, so N = G(B') = U_m G(B_{rho - 1/m}(c)) is a countable union of compact sets, hence Borel (SimonGMT Chapter03.measurableSet_of_isSigmaCompact_borel). By step 1 and the Lipschitz image bound (Simon Ch. 2, 1.8(i); SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn), H^n(N) <= Lambda^n H^n(B') = Lambda^n L^n(B') < infinity.
4. (Definition of T.) For x in N let T(x) := DG(psi(x))(R^n), the range of the derivative at the parameter of x; for x not in N let T(x) := {0}. For x in N, DG(psi(x)) is injective, so dim T(x) = n.
5. (Continuity of the projection field.) For v in B' let A(v) := DG(v) : R^n -> R^(n+l) and A(v)^* its adjoint. A(v)^*A(v) is invertible, since <A^*A h, h> = |A h|^2 > 0 for h != 0. Put P(v) := A(v)(A(v)^*A(v))^{-1}A(v)^*. Then P(v)y lies in range A(v), and for every h, <y - P(v)y, A(v)h> = <A(v)^*y - A(v)^*A(v)(A(v)^*A(v))^{-1}A(v)^*y, h> = 0; so y - P(v)y is orthogonal to range A(v) and P(v) is the orthogonal projection onto range A(v) (Submodule.starProjection of range A(v)). The maps v -> A(v) (continuity of DG), A -> A^* (a linear isometry) and inversion on the open set of invertible operators are continuous, so v -> P(v) is continuous on B'. Hence x -> p_{T(x)} = P(psi(x)) is continuous on N (step 2).
6. (Blow-up as a parametrized integral.) Fix x = G(w) in N (w in B'), r > 0, and f in C_c(R^(n+l)); let ||f|| := sup|f| and R > 0 with f = 0 outside B_R(0). Put Phi_r(s) := r^{-1}(G(w + r s) - G(w)) and B'_r := {s : w + r s in B'} (open, contains 0). Then eta_{x,r}(N) = Phi_r(B'_r); Phi_r is C^1 with DPhi_r(s) = DG(w + r s), injective for s in B'_r, and Phi_r is injective on B'_r (lower bound). By the area formula for injective maps with injective derivative (Simon Ch. 2, 3.2; SimonGMT Chapter02.integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative on the open, hence measurable, set B'_r, with H^n = L^n on R^n):
   int_{eta_{x,r}(N)} f dH^n = int_{B'_r} JG(w + r s) f(Phi_r(s)) ds.
7. (Dominated convergence.) Let g_r(s) := 1_{B'_r}(s) JG(w + r s) f(Phi_r(s)). (a) Pointwise: for fixed s, s lies in B'_r for all small r (B' open, w in B'), Phi_r(s) -> DG(w)s as r -> 0+ (differentiability of G at w), and JG(w + r s) -> JG(w) (continuity of JG); f is continuous, so g_r(s) -> JG(w) f(DG(w)s). (b) Domination: for s in B'_r, |Phi_r(s)| = r^{-1}|G(w + r s) - G(w)| >= kappa |s| (lower bound applied to w + r s and w in B'); hence f(Phi_r(s)) = 0 if |s| > R/kappa, and |g_r(s)| <= J* ||f|| 1{|s| <= R/kappa}, an integrable function independent of r (J* bounds JG(w + r s) because w + r s lies in B', which is contained in B). The filter r -> 0+ is countably generated, so by dominated convergence (Mathlib tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence)
   int_{eta_{x,r}(N)} f dH^n -> JG(w) int_{R^n} f(DG(w) s) ds as r -> 0+.
8. (Linear area formula.) For the injective linear map L := DG(w), the measure normDet(L) . L^n pushed forward by L equals H^n restricted to L(R^n) = T(x) (Simon Ch. 2, 3.1; SimonGMT Chapter02.measurePreserving_linearMap_normDet_smul / weighted_linear_area_formula), so JG(w) int_{R^n} f(L s) ds = int_{T(x)} f dH^n. With step 7, lim_{r -> 0+} int_{eta_{x,r}(N)} f dH^n = int_{T(x)} f dH^n for every f in C_c, and dim T(x) = n (step 4): T(x) is the approximate tangent space of N at x. Together with steps 3 and 5 this proves the claim.
proof_key_steps: DG is bounded on the closed ball, so G is Lipschitz on B' and JG is bounded
The lower bound makes G|B' injective with Lipschitz inverse psi on N
N is sigma-compact hence Borel, and H^n(N) <= Lambda^n L^n(B') < infinity
T(x) := DG(psi(x))(R^n) has dimension n; its projection A(A^*A)^{-1}A^* depends continuously on x in N
Area formula for the rescaled chart Phi_r turns the blow-up integral into int_{B'_r} JG(w+rs) f(Phi_r(s)) ds
Dominated convergence (support in |s| <= R/kappa by the lower bound) and the linear area formula give the limit int_{T(x)} f dH^n

audit.reason: The type exactly includes Borelness, finite measure, continuous orthogonal projections, and tangents at every image point. Global C¹ regularity bounds derivatives on the closed parameter ball; the lower bound supplies an inverse and uniform support control. The area formula and dominated convergence prove the exact tangent limit. The empty-ball case and projection continuity are covered.

subproblem.title: Weighted approximate tangent space forces density equal to multiplicity (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2))
subproblem.statement: Let n >= 1, U an open subset of R^(n+l), V = v(M, theta) a rectifiable n-varifold in U (contract structure RectifiableVarifold), x in M, and P a linear subspace which is the approximate tangent space of M with respect to theta at x (SimonGMT HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta x P). Then Theta^n(mu_V, x) = theta(x), i.e. V.HasDensity x (theta x): mu_V(B_r(x)) / (omega_n r^n) -> theta(x) as r -> 0+ (in [0, infinity], with mu_V = V.weight and omega_n = unitBallVolume n).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} {U : Set (Amb n ℓ)} (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (x : Amb n ℓ) (P : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)), 1 ≤ n → IsOpen U → x ∈ V.carrier → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n V.carrier V.mult x P → V.HasDensity x (V.mult x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 5 ('Density equals theta (Remark 1.8(2))'). Notation and conventions (shared): H^n = muHE[n] (Mathlib's normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure; on R^n it equals Lebesgue measure L^n = volume, Mathlib InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, and on an n-dimensional subspace P it is n-dimensional Lebesgue measure on P, so H^n(P cap B_s(0)) = omega_n s^n). Balls B_s(y) are closed, B'_s(y) open. eta_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y - x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). For r > 0, eta_{x,r} is a homeomorphism (a similarity with ratio 1/r), H^n(eta_{x,r}(S)) = r^{-n} H^n(S) for every set S, and the pushforward of H^n restricted to eta_{x,r}(S) under eta_{x,r}^{-1}(y) = x + r y is r^{-n} H^n restricted to S (SimonGMT Chapter04 hausdorff_blowUp_image, map_inverse_blowUp_carrier). Consequently, for every set S and every function h (Bochner integrals, the identity holding exactly, including the value 0 for non-integrable integrands, because it comes from a measurable embedding and a scalar multiple of a measure):
(CV) int_{eta_{x,r}(S)} h(y) dH^n(y) = r^{-n} int_S h(eta_{x,r}(z)) dH^n(z), and H^n(eta_{x,r}(S) cap B_R(0)) = r^{-n} H^n(S cap B_{rR}(x)).
mu := V.weight = ((H^n restricted to M) with density ENNReal.ofReal theta); omega_n := unitBallVolume n = pi^{n/2}/Gamma(n/2 + 1) > 0; theta(x) > 0 since x is in M; dim P = n by the first component of the hypothesis.
1. (Local finiteness.) x is in M, contained in the open set U; choose delta > 0 with B_{2 delta}(x) contained in U. For 0 < s <= 2 delta, mu(B_s(x)) = int_{M cap B_s(x)} theta dH^n < infinity by integrability of theta on M cap B_{2 delta}(x) (contract field integrableOn_mult; the closed ball is compact and contained in U).
2. (Cutoffs.) Fix e in (0, 1). Let f_+(y) := min(1, max(0, (1 + e - |y|)/e)) and f_-(y) := min(1, max(0, (1 - |y|)/e)). Both are continuous with compact support and values in [0, 1]; f_+ = 1 on B_1(0) and f_+ = 0 outside B_{1+e}(0); f_- = 1 on B_{1-e}(0) and f_- = 0 outside B_1(0). (SimonGMT's Chapter04 tangentDensityCutoff may be used for f_+.)
3. (Sandwich.) For 0 < r < delta and every z: f_-(eta_{x,r} z) <= 1_{B_r(x)}(z) <= f_+(eta_{x,r} z), since |eta_{x,r} z| = |z - x|/r. All three functions are bounded, Borel, and vanish outside B_{2r}(x), which has finite mu-measure (step 1); so they are mu-integrable and J_-(r) <= mu(B_r(x)) <= J_+(r), where J_pm(r) := int f_pm(eta_{x,r} z) dmu(z) are finite real numbers (mu(B_r(x)) is read as a real number).
4. (Change of variables.) For 0 < r < delta: J_pm(r) = int_M f_pm(eta_{x,r} z) theta(z) dH^n(z), by the Bochner integral formula for a measure with a.e.-measurable finite density (Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀) and toReal(ofReal theta(z)) = theta(z) for z in M (theta > 0 on M; M is H^n-null-measurable, so H^n-a.e. point of the restricted measure lies in M). By (CV) with h(y) := f_pm(y) theta(x + r y) and x + r eta_{x,r}(z) = z: J_pm(r) = r^n int_{eta_{x,r}(M)} f_pm(y) theta(x + r y) dH^n(y). By the hypothesis applied to f_pm in C_c(R^(n+l)): r^{-n} J_pm(r) -> theta(x) int_P f_pm dH^n as r -> 0+.
5. (Plane integrals.) H^n restricted to P is n-dimensional Lebesgue measure on P, so H^n(P cap B_s(0)) = omega_n s^n for s > 0 (SimonGMT Chapter04.planeMeasure_unit_closedBall together with the scaling H^n(lambda S) = lambda^n H^n(S); or Mathlib InnerProductSpace.volume_closedBall on P, which is isometric to R^n). Since 1_{B_{1-e}(0)} <= f_- and f_+ <= 1_{B_{1+e}(0)}: omega_n (1 - e)^n <= int_P f_- dH^n and int_P f_+ dH^n <= omega_n (1 + e)^n.
6. (Limit.) From steps 3-5 and theta(x) > 0: liminf_{r -> 0+} r^{-n} mu(B_r(x)) >= theta(x) omega_n (1 - e)^n and limsup_{r -> 0+} r^{-n} mu(B_r(x)) <= theta(x) omega_n (1 + e)^n. Since e in (0, 1) is arbitrary, r^{-n} mu(B_r(x)) -> theta(x) omega_n, i.e. mu(B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) -> theta(x) (omega_n > 0).
7. (Extended reals.) For 0 < r < delta, mu(B_r(x)) < infinity and omega_n r^n > 0, so V.weight(B_r(x)) / ENNReal.ofReal(omega_n r^n) = ENNReal.ofReal(mu(B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n)) with mu(B_r(x)) read as a real number. By continuity of ENNReal.ofReal and step 6 this tends to ENNReal.ofReal(theta(x)) along r -> 0+, which is V.HasDensity x (theta x).
proof_key_steps: mu is finite on small closed balls around x (x in M contained in U open, theta locally integrable)
Continuous cutoffs f_- <= indicator of the unit ball <= f_+ with supports in B_1 and B_{1+e}
Change of variables: r^{-n} int f_pm(eta_{x,r} z) dmu(z) equals the weighted blow-up integral, which converges to theta(x) int_P f_pm
H^n(P cap B_s(0)) = omega_n s^n bounds the plane integrals between omega_n(1-e)^n and omega_n(1+e)^n
Squeeze, let e -> 0, and transfer the real limit to the extended-real density quotient

audit.reason: The type matches the pointwise density assertion and includes carrier membership. Local integrability ensures finite small-ball masses; the two explicit cutoffs sandwich them. The weighted change of variables and plane normalization yield the real density limit, and the final ENNReal conversion proves precisely V.HasDensity. The proof uses only the supplied tangent hypothesis and established measure facts.

subproblem.title: Weighted approximate tangent at H^n-a.e. point of a continuity piece of a chart (proof of Simon Ch. 3, 1.6 'only if', and Remark 1.8(1))
subproblem.statement: Let n >= 1, U an open subset of R^(n+l), and V = v(M, theta) a rectifiable n-varifold in U (contract structure RectifiableVarifold). Let C be a compact set contained in M with theta restricted to C continuous, N a Borel set with H^n(N) < infinity, and T a map from R^(n+l) to the linear subspaces of R^(n+l) such that for every x in N, T(x) is the approximate tangent space of N at x (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x (T x), Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4). Then for H^n-a.e. x in C cap N, T(x) is the approximate tangent space of M with respect to theta at x (SimonGMT HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta x (T x), Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.7): dim T(x) = n and lim_{r -> 0+} int_{eta_{x,r}(M)} f(y) theta(x + r y) dH^n(y) = theta(x) int_{T(x)} f dH^n for every f in C_c(R^(n+l)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} {U : Set (Amb n ℓ)} (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (C N : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (T : Amb n ℓ → Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)), 1 ≤ n → IsOpen U → IsCompact C → C ⊆ V.carrier → ContinuousOn V.mult C → MeasurableSet N → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) N < ⊤ → (∀ x ∈ N, Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x (T x)) → ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)).restrict (C ∩ N)), Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n V.carrier V.mult x (T x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 4 ('Tangent spaces at good points', proof of Simon 1.6 'only if' with Remark 1.8(1)), with the parent's piece C_{m,i,k} = C_{m,i} cap M_k replaced by C' := C cap N and the parent's finite measure mu_m by mu restricted to a compact neighbourhood K' of C in U. Notation and conventions (shared): H^n = muHE[n] (Mathlib's normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure; on R^n it equals Lebesgue measure L^n = volume, Mathlib InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, and on an n-dimensional subspace P it is n-dimensional Lebesgue measure on P, so H^n(P cap B_s(0)) = omega_n s^n). Balls B_s(y) are closed, B'_s(y) open. eta_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y - x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). For r > 0, eta_{x,r} is a homeomorphism (a similarity with ratio 1/r), H^n(eta_{x,r}(S)) = r^{-n} H^n(S) for every set S, and the pushforward of H^n restricted to eta_{x,r}(S) under eta_{x,r}^{-1}(y) = x + r y is r^{-n} H^n restricted to S (SimonGMT Chapter04 hausdorff_blowUp_image, map_inverse_blowUp_carrier). Consequently, for every set S and every function h (Bochner integrals, the identity holding exactly, including the value 0 for non-integrable integrands, because it comes from a measurable embedding and a scalar multiple of a measure):
(CV) int_{eta_{x,r}(S)} h(y) dH^n(y) = r^{-n} int_S h(eta_{x,r}(z)) dH^n(z), and H^n(eta_{x,r}(S) cap B_R(0)) = r^{-n} H^n(S cap B_{rR}(x)).
Write mu := V.weight = theta H^n restricted to M, C' := C cap N (Borel, contained in M and in N), ||f|| := sup|f|.
1. (Compact neighbourhood.) If C is empty there is nothing to prove. C is compact and contained in the open set U (C contained in M contained in U), so there is delta > 0 with K' := {y : dist(y, C) <= delta} contained in U (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open); K' is closed and bounded, hence compact. Since theta is integrable on M cap K' (contract field integrableOn_mult), mu' := mu restricted to K' is a finite Borel measure; H^n restricted to N is a finite Borel measure (H^n(N) < infinity). Both are Borel regular in Simon's sense (SimonGMT Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular: the outer measure of a Borel measure is Borel regular).
2. (Upper Density Theorem.) By the Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6; SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6, whose Hausdorff measure simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n is a positive finite multiple of mu_H[n] by simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal_eq_scaled_hausdorffMeasure, as is muHE[n] by Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, so the two have the same null sets):
   (i) applied to H^n restricted to N and the Borel set N \ C': there is an H^n-null set E_1 such that for every x outside (N \ C') union E_1, rho^{-n} H^n((N \ C') cap B_rho(x)) -> 0 as rho -> 0+;
   (ii) applied to the finite Borel regular measure mu' and the Borel set R^(n+l) \ C' (finite mu'-measure): there is an H^n-null set E_2 such that for every x in C' \ E_2, rho^{-n} mu'((R^(n+l) \ C') cap B_rho(x)) -> 0 as rho -> 0+. Since mu' is carried by M (mu'(S) = mu'(S cap M) for every set S), mu'((R^(n+l) \ C') cap B_rho(x)) = mu'((M \ C') cap B_rho(x)); hence rho^{-n} mu'((M \ C') cap B_rho(x)) -> 0 for every x in C' \ E_2.
   E := E_1 union E_2 is H^n-null and does not depend on any test function. It suffices to prove the weighted tangent property at every x in C' \ E (the set of x in C' where it fails is then contained in E, hence H^n-null, which is the asserted a.e. statement for H^n restricted to C'). Fix such an x; x is not in N \ C', so both (i) and (ii) apply at x.
3. (Dimension.) x is in N, so dim T(x) = n by the hypothesis on N.
4. (Splitting.) Fix f in C_c(R^(n+l)) and R >= 1 with f = 0 outside B_R(0); let r_0 := delta/R, so that B_{rR}(x) is contained in K' for 0 < r < r_0 (x in C). For such r define I(r) := int_{eta_{x,r}(M)} f(y) theta(x + r y) dH^n(y). By (CV) with h(y) := f(y) theta(x + r y), and since x + r eta_{x,r}(z) = z:
   I(r) = r^{-n} int_M f(eta_{x,r} z) theta(z) dH^n(z).
   The integrand is a.e.-measurable for H^n restricted to M (theta is, f o eta_{x,r} is continuous), vanishes outside B_{rR}(x), contained in K', and is bounded by ||f|| theta 1_{K'}, which is integrable on M; so it is integrable and, as C' is contained in M, I(r) = I_1(r) + theta(x) I_2(r) + I_3(r) with
   I_1(r) := r^{-n} int_{M \ C'} f(eta_{x,r} z) theta(z) dH^n(z), I_2(r) := r^{-n} int_{C'} f(eta_{x,r} z) dH^n(z), I_3(r) := r^{-n} int_{C'} f(eta_{x,r} z)(theta(z) - theta(x)) dH^n(z)
   (all finite: f o eta is bounded, H^n(C') <= H^n(N) < infinity, theta is integrable on C', contained in M cap K').
5. (I_1 -> 0.) |I_1(r)| <= ||f|| r^{-n} int_{(M \ C') cap B_{rR}(x)} theta dH^n = ||f|| r^{-n} mu'((M \ C') cap B_{rR}(x)) = ||f|| R^n (rR)^{-n} mu'((M \ C') cap B_{rR}(x)) -> 0 by 2(ii).
6. (I_2 -> int_{T(x)} f.) By (CV), I_2(r) = int_{eta_{x,r}(C')} f dH^n. eta_{x,r}(N) is the disjoint union of the Borel sets eta_{x,r}(C') and eta_{x,r}(N \ C') and has finite measure r^{-n}H^n(N), so I_2(r) = int_{eta_{x,r}(N)} f dH^n - int_{eta_{x,r}(N \ C')} f dH^n. The first term tends to int_{T(x)} f dH^n because T(x) is the approximate tangent space of N at x in N. For the second, |int_{eta_{x,r}(N \ C')} f dH^n| <= ||f|| H^n(eta_{x,r}(N \ C') cap B_R(0)) = ||f|| r^{-n} H^n((N \ C') cap B_{rR}(x)) = ||f|| R^n (rR)^{-n} H^n((N \ C') cap B_{rR}(x)) -> 0 by 2(i).
7. (Local mass bound.) Let phi in C_c(R^(n+l)) with 0 <= phi <= 1 and phi = 1 on B_R(0) (e.g. phi(y) = min(1, max(0, R + 1 - |y|))). Then r^{-n} H^n(C' cap B_{rR}(x)) <= r^{-n} H^n(N cap B_{rR}(x)) = H^n(eta_{x,r}(N) cap B_R(0)) <= int_{eta_{x,r}(N)} phi dH^n -> int_{T(x)} phi dH^n < infinity. Hence there are r_1 in (0, r_0) and Lambda < infinity with r^{-n} H^n(C' cap B_{rR}(x)) <= Lambda for 0 < r < r_1.
8. (I_3 -> 0.) Let omega(s) := sup{|theta(z) - theta(x)| : z in C, |z - x| <= s}; omega(s) -> 0 as s -> 0+ by continuity of theta restricted to C at x in C. For 0 < r < r_1, as f(eta_{x,r} z) = 0 unless |z - x| <= rR, |I_3(r)| <= ||f|| omega(rR) r^{-n} H^n(C' cap B_{rR}(x)) <= ||f|| Lambda omega(rR) -> 0.
9. (Conclusion.) By steps 4-8, I(r) -> theta(x) int_{T(x)} f dH^n as r -> 0+, for every f in C_c(R^(n+l)); with step 3 this is HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta x (T x). This holds for every x in C' \ E, hence for H^n-a.e. x in C cap N.
proof_key_steps: Choose a compact neighbourhood K' of C inside U; mu restricted to K' and H^n restricted to N are finite Borel measures
Upper Density Theorem twice: outside an H^n-null set E, N \ C' and M \ C' have zero n-density at points of C' = C cap N
Change of variables splits the weighted blow-up into the M \ C' part, theta(x) times the C' part, and the oscillation part
The M \ C' part vanishes in the limit by the density of mu' on M \ C'
The C' part converges to int_{T(x)} f because N has tangent T(x) and N \ C' has zero density
The oscillation part vanishes by continuity of theta on C and the local mass bound from the tangent of N

audit.reason: The prose states every hypothesis of the exact Lean proposition. Compact localization legitimizes both finite-measure density applications. Their exceptional sets are independent of test functions. The three-term decomposition, unweighted tangent limit, local mass bound, and continuity estimate prove the weighted limit for every test function, with integrability explicitly justified. No sibling conclusion is silently assumed.

subproblem.title: Lusin decomposition of the multiplicity into compact continuity pieces (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1), localized to U)
subproblem.statement: Let U be an open subset of R^(n+l) and V = v(M, theta) a rectifiable n-varifold in U in the sense of the contract structure RectifiableVarifold (M contained in U, H^n-null-measurable and countably n-rectifiable; theta > 0 on M; theta a.e.-measurable for H^n restricted to M; theta integrable on M cap K for every compact K contained in U). Then there are compact sets C_i (i in N), each contained in M, such that theta restricted to C_i is continuous for every i and H^n(M \ U_i C_i) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} {U : Set (Amb n ℓ)} (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U), IsOpen U → ∃ C : ℕ → Set (Amb n ℓ), (∀ i, IsCompact (C i) ∧ C i ⊆ V.carrier ∧ ContinuousOn V.mult (C i)) ∧ (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (V.carrier \ ⋃ i, C i) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 3 ('Lusin decomposition (Remark 1.8(1)), localized to U') and its measurability convention. H^n = muHE[n]; mu := V.weight = theta H^n restricted to M (density ENNReal.ofReal theta).
1. (Compact exhaustion.) U is an open subset of R^(n+l), hence sigma-compact: there are compact sets K_m (m in N) contained in U with U_m K_m = U (if U = R^(n+l) take K_m := B_m(0); otherwise K_m := {y in B_m(0) : dist(y, R^(n+l) \ U) >= 1/(m+1)}, which is closed, bounded and contained in U).
2. (Borel versions of M and theta.) Since theta is a.e.-measurable for H^n restricted to M, there is a Borel function g : R^(n+l) -> R with theta = g at H^n-a.e. point of M, i.e. H^n(M cap {theta != g}) = 0; choose a Borel H^n-null set Z' containing M cap {theta != g} (Mathlib exists_measurable_superset_of_null). Since M is H^n-null-measurable, choose a Borel set M' contained in M with H^n(M \ M') = 0 (Mathlib NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq). For m in N put A_m := (M' cap K_m) \ Z': a Borel subset of M on which theta = g.
3. (Finite measures.) nu_m := mu restricted to K_m is a finite Borel measure: nu_m(R^(n+l)) = int_{M cap K_m} theta dH^n < infinity because theta is integrable on M cap K_m (contract field integrableOn_mult, K_m compact and contained in U). A finite Borel measure on R^(n+l) is weakly regular (closed inner regular on Borel sets; Mathlib Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure).
4. (Lusin.) Fix m and i >= 1. By Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable) for nu_m, the Borel set A_m and the Borel function g, there is a closed set C_{m,i} contained in A_m with nu_m(A_m \ C_{m,i}) < 1/i and g restricted to C_{m,i} continuous. C_{m,i} is closed and contained in the compact set K_m, so it is compact; it is contained in A_m, hence in M; and theta = g on C_{m,i} (it avoids Z'), so theta restricted to C_{m,i} is continuous (ContinuousOn.congr).
5. (Null remainder on each K_m.) S_m := A_m \ U_i C_{m,i} is Borel and nu_m(S_m) <= nu_m(A_m \ C_{m,i}) < 1/i for all i, so 0 = nu_m(S_m) = mu(S_m) = int_{S_m} theta dH^n (S_m is contained in K_m and in M). As theta > 0 on S_m (S_m contained in M), this forces H^n(S_m) = 0: otherwise, with S_m^q := S_m cap {g > 1/q} (Borel, as theta = g on S_m), countable additivity gives some q with H^n(S_m^q) > 0, and then int_{S_m} theta dH^n >= H^n(S_m^q)/q > 0, a contradiction.
6. (Conclusion.) M is contained in U = U_m K_m, and M cap K_m is contained in (M \ M') union Z' union A_m, which is contained in (M \ M') union Z' union S_m union U_i C_{m,i}. Hence M \ U_{m,i} C_{m,i} is contained in (M \ M') union Z' union U_m S_m, a countable union of H^n-null sets, so it is H^n-null. Finally enumerate the pairs (m, i) by k in N (k -> Nat.unpair k, using C_{m,0} := C_{m,1} for i = 0) to obtain the family (C_k) of the statement.
proof_key_steps: Exhaust the open set U by compact sets K_m
Replace M and theta by Borel versions M' and g off an H^n-null set
mu restricted to K_m is a finite, weakly regular Borel measure (local integrability of theta)
Lusin: closed, hence compact, C_{m,i} contained in M with theta continuous on C_{m,i} and small leftover mass
The leftover S_m is mu-null; since theta > 0 on M it is H^n-null
Collect the countably many pieces C_{m,i}; the uncovered part of M is H^n-null

audit.reason: The statement and type agree for arbitrary natural dimensions. Borel representatives handle the null-measurable carrier and a.e.-measurable multiplicity correctly. Compact exhaustion makes each restricted weight finite; Lusin yields compact continuity pieces. Strict positivity converts the remaining weight-null sets into Hausdorff-null sets. No global integrability or tangent theorem is assumed.

subproblem.title: Countably rectifiable sets are covered by bi-Lipschitz C^1 chart images (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 'only if', Remark 1.3)
subproblem.statement: Let n >= 1, l >= 0 and let M be a countably n-rectifiable subset of R^(n+l) (SimonGMT Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable n M: M is contained in M_0 union U_j F_j(R^n) with H^n(M_0) = 0 and F_j : R^n -> R^(n+l) Lipschitz). Then there are a set N_0 with H^n(N_0) = 0 and, for k in N, C^1 maps G_k : R^n -> R^(n+l), centres c_k in R^n and radii rho_k in R such that, writing B'_k for the open ball B'_{rho_k}(c_k): (i) DG_k(v) is injective for every v in B'_k; (ii) there is kappa_k > 0 with kappa_k |v - w| <= |G_k(v) - G_k(w)| for all v, w in B'_k; and (iii) M is contained in N_0 union U_k G_k(B'_k).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} (M : Set (Amb n ℓ)), 1 ≤ n → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable n M → ∃ (N₀ : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (G : ℕ → Rn n → Amb n ℓ) (c : ℕ → Rn n) (ρ : ℕ → ℝ), (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) N₀ = 0 ∧ (∀ k, ContDiff ℝ 1 (G k)) ∧ (∀ k, ∀ v ∈ ball (c k) (ρ k), Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ (G k) v)) ∧ (∀ k, ∃ κ : ℝ, 0 < κ ∧ ∀ v ∈ ball (c k) (ρ k), ∀ w ∈ ball (c k) (ρ k), κ * ‖v - w‖ ≤ ‖G k v - G k w‖) ∧ M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃ k, G k '' ball (c k) (ρ k)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 1 (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 'only if' and Remark 1.3), in the chart form needed later. H^n = muHE[n]; on R^n, H^n = L^n (Mathlib InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume together with finrank (EuclideanSpace R (Fin n)) = n). N := n + l >= 1.
1. (Definition.) By hypothesis there are M_0 with H^n(M_0) = 0 and Lipschitz maps F_j : R^n -> R^N (j in N), F_j with constant L_j, such that M is contained in M_0 union U_j F_j(R^n).
2. (C^1 approximation.) Fix j and i >= 1. For each coordinate q = 1, ..., N the function F_j^q := (x -> F_j(x)_q) is L_j-Lipschitz (coordinate projections of EuclideanSpace are 1-Lipschitz). By the sibling theorem tae_lipschitz_c1_approximation (Simon Ch. 2, Thm 1.5) there is a C^1 function g_{ij}^q : R^n -> R with L^n({F_j^q != g_{ij}^q}) < 1/(i N). Let G_{ij} : R^n -> R^N be the map with coordinates g_{ij}^1, ..., g_{ij}^N; it is C^1 (a map into EuclideanSpace is C^1 iff its coordinates are), and {F_j != G_{ij}} is contained in U_q {F_j^q != g_{ij}^q}, so L^n({F_j != G_{ij}}) < 1/i.
3. (Null remainder.) Let Z_j := intersection over i >= 1 of {F_j != G_{ij}} = R^n \ U_i {F_j = G_{ij}}. Then L^n(Z_j) <= L^n({F_j != G_{ij}}) < 1/i for all i, so L^n(Z_j) = 0. As F_j is L_j-Lipschitz, H^n(F_j(Z_j)) <= L_j^n H^n(Z_j) = L_j^n L^n(Z_j) = 0 (Simon Ch. 2, 1.8(i); SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn). If v is not in Z_j there is i with F_j(v) = G_{ij}(v). Hence F_j(R^n) is contained in F_j(Z_j) union U_i G_{ij}(R^n).
4. (Critical points.) Fix i, j and write G := G_{ij}; G is differentiable everywhere. Let Crit := {v : DG(v) is not injective}. By the critical-image theorem (the area-formula argument of Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.2; SimonGMT Chapter02.area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero, whose measure is muHE[finrank R (R^n)] = H^n), H^n(G(Crit)) = 0. The set O := {v : DG(v) injective} = R^n \ Crit is open: v -> DG(v) is continuous, and if L : R^n -> R^N is injective with c := min_{|e| = 1} |L e| > 0 (unit sphere compact, n >= 1), then every L' with ||L' - L|| < c satisfies |L' e| >= c - ||L' - L|| > 0 for |e| = 1, so L' is injective.
5. (Bi-Lipschitz balls.) Let w_0 in O, L := DG(w_0) and c_0 := min_{|e| = 1} |L e| > 0, so |L h| >= c_0 |h| for all h. By continuity of DG choose delta > 0 with ||DG(v) - L|| <= c_0/2 whenever |v - w_0| < delta, and put B' := B'_delta(w_0). (a) For v in B' and h in R^n: |DG(v) h| >= |L h| - ||DG(v) - L|| |h| >= (c_0/2)|h|, so DG(v) is injective. (b) For v, w in B': the C^1 map H(u) := G(u) - L u has ||DH(u)|| = ||DG(u) - L|| <= c_0/2 on the convex set B', so by the mean value inequality |H(v) - H(w)| <= (c_0/2)|v - w|; hence |G(v) - G(w)| >= |L(v - w)| - |H(v) - H(w)| >= (c_0/2)|v - w|. Thus (i) and (ii) hold on B' with kappa = c_0/2 > 0.
6. (Lindelof.) The open set O is covered by the balls B'(w_0), w_0 in O, from step 5. Since R^n is second countable, countably many of them, B'_{ij,m} = B'_{delta_{ij,m}}(w_{ij,m}), m in N, already cover O (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable); if O is empty use balls of radius 0 (empty), for which (i) and (ii) hold vacuously with kappa = 1. Hence G_{ij}(R^n) is contained in G_{ij}(Crit_{ij}) union U_m G_{ij}(B'_{ij,m}).
7. (Assembly.) Let N_0 := M_0 union U_j F_j(Z_j) union U_{i,j} G_{ij}(Crit_{ij}); it is a countable union of H^n-null sets, so H^n(N_0) = 0. Enumerate the countable index set of triples (i, j, m) by k in N (via a bijection N -> N^3, e.g. iterated Nat.unpair) and set G_k := G_{ij}, c_k := w_{ij,m}, rho_k := delta_{ij,m}. Each G_k is C^1 and satisfies (i), (ii) on B'_k by steps 5-6. Finally, by steps 1, 3, 4, 6: M is contained in M_0 union U_j F_j(R^n), which is contained in M_0 union U_j F_j(Z_j) union U_{i,j} G_{ij}(R^n), which is contained in N_0 union U_{i,j,m} G_{ij}(B'_{ij,m}) = N_0 union U_k G_k(B'_k). This is (iii).
